text:
ana: FYI seeing a big pile of tiny-gpu pods Pending in ap-southeast1 for ~90m. Counts creeping to ~380. Many nodes show 0.125 slots free but scheduler says affinity mismatch.
rico: Any common selector?
ana: (typo) ana: Most of them have nodeAffinity required to `socket-local: true` (apps need same NUMA socket for micro-batching). New racks deployed yesterday advertise `socket=dual` but inventory labels are `socket=shared` on half of them.
tess: So scheduler treats them as not matching and leaves them Pending even though there are enough free fractional GPUs.
vince: Pod describe shows: `0/176 nodes are available: 176 node(s) didn't match pod affinity/selector, 24 node(s) had taint {gpu:isolated=true:NoSchedule}`.
ops-bot: [automated] ap-southeast1 conntrack usage: 63% (warn 80%). Node allocatable GPU slots: total 512, free fractional slots 142.
rico: How did the labels diverge? did the cloud inventory job skip the new racks?
ana: (ana) inventory sync job errored during rollout due to a flaky metadata API; nodes fell back to default labeling.
tess: Short-term options: 1) label nodes correctly (clean) 2) relax pod affinity for single-container <1 GPU jobs via mutating webhook 3) add toleration for gpu:isolated on tiny pods so they can schedule on tainted nodes if safe.
vince: Warning: tolerating gpu:isolated could surface to big-gang jobs that actually need isolation. We must gate by annotation.
rico: Proposed quick mitigation: deploy a namespace-scoped mutating webhook that looks for annotation `redwood.fractional=true` and rewrites requiredDuringScheduling to preferredDuringScheduling for socket-local affinity. Limit to single-container, cpu <2, gpu <1.
ops-bot: [automated] Suggestion: drain-based relabeling could work: run `inv-sync --repair --pool=ap-east-mixed` but that triggers pod evictions during repair.
nana: I want minimal blast radius. Plan I propose:
- Step 0: bump cluster-autoscaler stabilization to 6m
- Step 1: deploy webhook to canary namespace `tiny-gpu-canary` only (10% of traffic)
- Step 2: if canary schedules cleanly for 15m, expand to tiny-gpu-prod namespaces
- Step 3: once pressure eases, run inventory relabel job during low traffic window and remove webhook
- Step 4: add CI scheduler test for `socket-local` + mixed-pool labels
ric o: +1. I'll write the webhook patch.
tess: Also add a metric for "fractional scheduling latency" and alert at 120s p95.
ops-bot: [automated] Noted: conntrack below threshold but we should throttle model-proxy sidecars on fractional pods. Top consumers in ap-southeast1: model-proxy 68%, metrics 15%.
mei: Can we instead create a soft-scheduler policy that gives weight to `socket=shared` so pods can fall back rather than mutate pod specs? That avoids mutating runtime YAMLs.
nana: Weighting is nice but requires scheduler rollout and policy change across clusters; takes longer. Webhook quick, then follow with scheduler policy.
vince: Operational safety checklist: mark webhook reversible (feature flag), run canary, autoscaler cooldown, conntrack watch, and remove any tolerations after relabel.
nana: I'll coordinate and run the canary in 12m. Rico, ping me when patch is ready.
rico: Will do. Pushing draft webhook in 8m.
tess: After we finish, follow-ups: - fix inventory sync root cause - add node-label admission guard to prevent future label drift - consider background defragmenter that consolidates tiny pods during slack windows to reduce fragmentation cost.
mei: Also capture cost impact: fractional pods waiting adds GPU-minutes waste if nodes stay warm; set a dashboard.
nana: Thanks everyone. Keep updates here; if canary fails, revert webhook immediately and we proceed to node relabel remediation. :pray:
